title: Chapter 7 Mastery Quiz: The Cognitive Revolution & Neuropsychology
description: Demonstrate comprehensive mastery of Tolman, Chomsky, information processing, Miller's 7±2, Neisser, Hebb, and Patient H.M.

questions.question: What behaviorist assumption was disproven by Edward Tolman's latent learning experiments with rats?

options.text: That learning requires immediate, explicit reinforcement to occur
That animals can speak human words
That food is satisfying to hungry animals

questions.explanation: Tolman proved that rats form cognitive maps during unrewarded exploration, demonstrating that learning can occur without reinforcement.

questions.question: What term did Edward Tolman use to describe an internal mental representation of environmental layout?
questions.explanation: Tolman introduced the concept of the 'cognitive map' to explain spatial orientation and latent learning.

questions.question: What 1957 book by B.F. Skinner attempted to explain all human language through operant conditioning?
questions.explanation: Skinner's 'Verbal Behavior' (1957) applied operant conditioning to human speech and grammar.

questions.question: Who published the devastating 1959 critique of Skinner's 'Verbal Behavior' that helped launch the Cognitive Revolution?
questions.explanation: Linguist Noam Chomsky's 1959 review demonstrated the logical fallacies of reducing language to operant conditioning.

questions.question: What argument did Noam Chomsky use regarding the 'Poverty of the Stimulus'?

options.text: Children hear finite, imperfect speech examples yet generate infinite novel, grammatically correct sentences
Poor families never speak to their children
Language cannot be spoken without monetary reward
Animal communication is more complex than human language

questions.explanation: Poverty of the stimulus points out that input speech is too impoverished to explain children's rapid mastery of complex syntax without innate mechanisms.

questions.question: What innate biological mechanism did Chomsky propose that enables children to rapidly acquire language?
questions.explanation: Chomsky hypothesized an innate Language Acquisition Device (LAD) containing Universal Grammar.

questions.question: What central metaphor did cognitive psychology adopt during the 1950s to model mental processes?

options.text: The mind as a computer (hardware/brain, software/mind)
The mind as a steam engine
The mind as a tabula rasa

questions.explanation: Cognitive psychology adopted the computer metaphor, analyzing information flow: encoding, storage, and retrieval.

questions.question: Who published 'Perception and Communication' (1958), introducing the first formal filter model of selective attention?
questions.explanation: Donald Broadbent introduced the filter model of selective attention based on dichotic listening experiments.

questions.question: In a dichotic listening task, what are experimental participants instructed to do?

options.text: Listen to different auditory messages presented simultaneously to each ear and shadow (repeat aloud) one message
Look at two flashing lights while tapping their feet
Condition a dog to salivate to tones

questions.explanation: Dichotic listening presents competing audio streams to both ears, requiring the participant to shadow one target channel.

questions.question: What modification did Anne Treisman propose to Broadbent's filter model to explain how people hear their own name at loud parties?

options.text: The Attenuation Model: unattended signals are weakened (volume turned down) rather than completely blocked
The brain only processes visual signals, never sound

questions.explanation: Treisman's Attenuation Model posits that unattended messages are attenuated rather than entirely filtered out, allowing salient stimuli through.

questions.question: What did George A. Miller proclaim as the 'Magical Number' representing human short-term memory capacity?
questions.explanation: Miller established that short-term memory can hold approximately 7 ± 2 items (5 to 9 units) of information.

questions.question: How does the cognitive strategy of 'chunking' bypass the 7 ± 2 item limit of short-term memory?

options.text: It recodes individual items into larger, meaningful conceptual units
It destroys old memories to make room for new ones
It uses hypnosis to expand brain capacity
It converts auditory sounds into tactile vibrations

questions.explanation: Chunking reorganizes information into familiar units, allowing each of the 7 memory slots to store much richer data.

questions.question: Who authored the 1967 landmark textbook titled 'Cognitive Psychology', officially naming and defining the discipline?
questions.explanation: Ulric Neisser published 'Cognitive Psychology' in 1967, providing the unified charter for the cognitive revolution.

questions.question: What did Ulric Neisser mean when he called for greater 'Ecological Validity' in psychological research?

options.text: Studies should investigate how cognitive processes operate in real-world everyday contexts, not just sterile labs
Psychologists should recycle paper in their offices
Research must focus solely on plant biology
All testing should be conducted underwater

questions.explanation: Ecological validity requires that experimental findings be generalizable to real-world natural settings.

questions.question: What famous phrase summarizes Donald Hebb's 1949 neurophysiological rule of learning?

options.text: 'The whole is other than the sum of parts'

questions.explanation: Hebb's rule is universally summarized as 'Neurons that fire together, wire together' (synaptic co-activation strengthens connection).

questions.question: What cellular biological phenomenon discovered in 1973 confirmed Donald Hebb's theoretical synaptic learning model?
questions.explanation: Long-Term Potentiation (LTP) demonstrates persistent synaptic strengthening following high-frequency stimulation, validating Hebbian plasticity.

questions.question: Why did neurosurgeon William Scoville resect both medial temporal lobes in Patient H.M. (Henry Molaison) in 1953?

options.text: To treat severe, uncontrollable epileptic seizures
To cure a malignant brain tumor

questions.explanation: The bilateral medial temporal lobectomy was performed as a desperate measure to relieve incapacitating epileptic seizures.

questions.question: What primary cognitive deficit afflicted Patient H.M. following his 1953 surgery?

options.text: Severe anterograde amnesia (inability to form new declarative long-term memories)
Total loss of spoken language (Broca's aphasia)
Loss of all childhood memories prior to surgery

questions.explanation: H.M. suffered dense anterograde amnesia: he could no longer consolidate new conscious experiences into long-term memory.

questions.question: What did Brenda Milner discover when she tested Patient H.M. on the mirror-tracing task over several days?

options.text: His motor drawing skill improved normally, despite having zero conscious recollection of ever doing the task before
He was physically unable to hold a pencil
His memory improved and cured his amnesia
He forgot how to speak English

questions.explanation: Milner showed that H.M. learned motor skills flawlessly, proving a double dissociation between declarative and procedural memory systems.

questions.question: Which brain structure, removed from Patient H.M., is essential for consolidating conscious explicit memories?
questions.explanation: The hippocampus (part of the medial temporal lobe) is critical for converting short-term declarative memories into long-term storage.

questions.question: How did Saul Sternberg use reaction times in the 1960s to study short-term memory retrieval?

options.text: He demonstrated that people search items in short-term memory via serial, exhaustive scanning
He showed that reaction times never vary
He proved that memory is instantaneous like electricity
He showed that animals react faster than humans

questions.explanation: Sternberg's memory scanning task showed linear reaction time increases per added memory item, indicating serial scanning.

questions.question: What is the defining triumph of the Cognitive Revolution over behaviorism?

options.text: It demonstrated that internal mental processes can be studied scientifically, quantitatively, and objectively
It proved that animals have no brain
It returned psychology to 17th-century armchair philosophy

questions.explanation: The cognitive revolution proved that complex mental operations (attention, memory, problem-solving, language) can be objectively measured with mathematical and experimental rigor.
